data.headline: Leveraged funds turn net short Nasdaq-100 futures
data.summary: Leveraged funds moved from a net long of 13,967 Nasdaq-100 futures contracts on November 10 to a net short of 10,928 on November 17. Asset managers increased their net long during the same week.

bull.text: Asset managers’ net long rose to 82,900 contracts from 72,785. Their exposure increased while leveraged funds crossed to the short side.

bear.text: The leveraged-fund balance swung 24,895 contracts toward the short side. The category ended the week holding more short contracts than long contracts.

watch.text: The ten-year Treasury yield fell from 5.04% to 4.92% between November 19 and 20. That matters to valuations based on distant earnings, and the rate move came after the positioning snapshot.

limitations: The CFTC counts Nasdaq-100 futures contracts. It cannot establish an individual fund’s intent or QQQ share flows. Monday’s QQQ price response and current options exposure remain unmeasured here.
